before: white-space controls how whitespace and wrapping are handled. normal permits ordinary wrapping; nowrap prevents it. overflow-wrap: anywhere permits breaks inside otherwise unbreakable text when needed to prevent overflow. It does not delete letters.

The rule makes a long label readable in a narrow box without clipping it. overflow-wrap cannot override nowrap’s prohibition on wrapping; allow wrapping first. This differs from overflow:hidden, which can hide excess content rather than putting it on additional lines.

after: Wrapping means moving text onto another line when it runs out of room. `white-space: normal` allows normal wrapping. `white-space: nowrap` keeps it on one line.
`overflow-wrap: anywhere` lets the browser break a long word when needed to stop it from sticking out. It keeps every letter. This works only when wrapping is allowed.
